summary: New full D1-D8 review of the single-runtime requirements cycle, based on direct reading of the complete candidate, amended PRD, S1-S4, inherited specifications, and cited sources at baseline 775bd5fa974f1008bb24e71ea92f674515706948. The actual hash matches the brief; no open-questions.md exists. Sections 2-3 retain boot-time installer ownership and data-only backend wiring without a new reverse dependency. Sections 0, 4, 8, and 13 explicitly override the parent's multi-version and completed-manifest cleanup rules, exclude generation/history infrastructure, and keep runtime-id as metadata. Sections 4 and 8 match full versions/platform/artifact digests/worker identity rather than relying on the abbreviated id. Preparation preserves runtime/; stopped, invocation-owned staging is reclaimable without a manifest, while foreign/crashed staging is untouched. Under proposed A8, section 8's closed-handle removal and same-filesystem rename to an absent path are feasible on Windows and Unix; it does not claim atomic overwrite or old-or-new crash durability. A9 explicitly exposes retirement, deletion, rename, sync, and validation failure states without fallback or backup. Sections 5-8 and 10 agree on missing tools, checksum/metadata failures, replacement outcomes, cleanup precedence, and pre-retirement-only download retry. Section 11 gives offline landing points for AC1-AC6: installation/reuse, fixed-path identity replacement, corruption/mismatch reinstall, failed preparation preserving prior bytes, no-prior-install failure, manifest-free cleanup and foreign-path retention, publication/restart failures, single-commit history, and frozen contract gates. Numbered sections remain addressable; no broad refactor or hidden updater framework is introduced. No blocking gap was found. This is document-level PASS, not implementation acceptance or approval of A8/A9. Their behavior is specified sufficiently for review, but the owner must decide their deployment and availability tradeoffs before a new lock. No Cargo command, build, test suite, acceptance-history procedure, commit, or subagent was run; approval.md was not modified.

The retained-archive policy explicitly does not detect arbitrary edits inside an otherwise present extracted Python tree; sections 8 and 11 do not disguise that limitation as full-tree validation.

A7: Retired, not pending and not approved. Design.md section 0, lines 33-49; section 8, lines 499-511; and section 12, lines 735-738, implement S2/S3 and amended PRD requirement 3: a completed manifest is not required to remove this invocation's contained, quiescent temporary work. Active inline count: 0. The previous manifest-prerequisite policy must not be restored from the historical round-4 PASS.

A8: NEW proposal requiring owner confirmation before implementation lock. Inline location: design.md section 8, lines 388-400. Section-12 entry: lines 739-743. Inline count: 1. One canonical libs-dir is private to one wrapper instance for its full serving lifetime; deployment stops and awaits prior consumers/children before startup. The root is local and runtime/staging are ordinary same-filesystem directories; runtime/ is reserved installer-owned content even with damaged metadata. This is an operator precondition, not automatic concurrency protection. Shared-root rolling starts are outside the proposal. The replacement safety argument depends on this precondition; PASS does not establish that existing deployments satisfy it.

A9: NEW proposal requiring owner confirmation before implementation lock. Inline location: design.md section 8, lines 448-455. Section-12 entry: lines 744-748. Inline count: 1. After full verified preparation, invalidate the old manifest, remove the old tree, and rename to the absent fixed path without backup/restore. Failed preparation preserves the prior bytes; after retirement starts, a failure or abrupt death may leave an invalid remainder or no runtime and require a later staged reinstall. Section 8 explicitly separates Unix directory sync from Windows behavior and disclaims a portable power-loss transaction. This materially trades post-preparation availability for a simpler single-install lifecycle. The owner must accept or reject that tradeoff; this review neither approves it nor authorizes destructive publication.

All eight active assumptions A1-A6/A8-A9 have exactly one inline marker and matching section-12 entries. No additional blocking unmarked decision or unresolved behavioral branch was found. A8/A9 need an owner decision before re-locking, but their explicit proposed semantics permit document review without inventing a locking, history, or recovery subsystem. The historical approval record is not an implementation authorization for this candidate.
